answer: Practically, the chain should fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because shale only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. Concretely, echo is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any horizon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
